newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope issues fresh appeal for Great Lakes region.
newsitem.headline: Pope issues fresh appeal for Great Lakes region.

text.p: Pope John Paul issued a fresh call for peace in the Great Lakes region of Africa on Saturday and said the world should do more to end the human suffering caused by fighting there.

"Dialogue and negotiation must replace conflict in the resolution of tensions. The need is especially urgent in the Great Lakes region, where violence and bloodshed continue to cause untold suffering and claim countless victims.
"Neither Africa nor the larger family of nations can turn a deaf ear to the cries of the men, women and children whose lives are being destroyed in these fraticidal conflicts," the Pope said.
He was speaking in address to the new ambassador to the Vatican for Tanzania, which he praised for receiving refugees from neighbouring countries.

The Pope, 76, has made frequent appeals for peace in the Great Lakes region and international action in support of refugees and people displaced by killing in Rwanda and Burundi, which have a similar ethnic mix, as well as Zaire.
"There is no question that much is being done especially by voluntary aid organisations and by the international community but much more is still needed," the Pope said.

He told the envoy, Andrew Mhando Daraja, that Africa had to continue on the path to democratisation and that he hoped a new Secretariat for East African Cooperation which was recently set up would help foster partnership and development in the region.
